text: All the while my breath [is] in me, and the spirit of God [is] in my nostrils; {the spirit...: that is, the breath which God gave him}

title: Job 27:4
text: My lips shall not speak wickedness, nor my tongue utter deceit.

title: Job 27:5
text: God forbid that I should justify you: till I die I will not remove mine integrity from me.

title: Job 27:6
text: My righteousness I hold fast, and will not let it go: my heart shall not reproach [me] so long as I live. {so long...: Heb. from my days}

title: Job 27:7
text: ¶Let mine enemy be as the wicked, and he that riseth up against me as the unrighteous.

title: Job 27:8
text: For what [is] the hope of the hypocrite, though he hath gained, when God taketh away his soul?

title: Job 27:9
text: Will God hear his cry when trouble cometh upon him?

title: Job 27:10
text: Will he delight himself in the Almighty? will he always call upon God?

title: Job 27:11
text: ¶I will teach you by the hand of God: [that] which [is] with the Almighty will I not conceal. {by...: or, being in the hand, etc}

title: Job 27:12
text: Behold, all ye yourselves have seen [it]; why then are ye thus altogether vain?

title: Job 27:13
text: This [is] the portion of a wicked man with God, and the heritage of oppressors, [which] they shall receive of the Almighty.

title: Job 27:14
text: If his children be multiplied, [it is] for the sword: and his offspring shall not be satisfied with bread.

title: Job 27:15
text: Those that remain of him shall be buried in death: and his widows shall not weep.

title: Job 27:16
text: Though he heap up silver as the dust, and prepare raiment as the clay;

title: Job 27:17
text: He may prepare [it], but the just shall put [it] on, and the innocent shall divide the silver.

title: Job 27:18
text: He buildeth his house as a moth, and as a booth [that] the keeper maketh.

title: Job 27:19
text: The rich man shall lie down, but he shall not be gathered: he openeth his eyes, and he [is] not.

title: Job 27:20
text: Terrors take hold on him as waters, a tempest stealeth him away in the night.

title: Job 27:21
text: The east wind carrieth him away, and he departeth: and as a storm hurleth him out of his place.

title: Job 27:22
text: For [God] shall cast upon him, and not spare: he would fain flee out of his hand. {he...: Heb. in fleeing he would flee}

title: Job 27:23
text: [Men] shall clap their hands at him, and shall hiss him out of his place.

title: Job 28:1
text: ¶Surely there is a vein for the silver, and a place for gold [where] they fine [it]. {vein: or, mine}

title: Job 28:2
text: Iron is taken out of the earth, and brass [is] molten [out of] the stone. {earth: or, dust}

title: Job 28:3
text: He setteth an end to darkness, and searcheth out all perfection: the stones of darkness, and the shadow of death.

title: Job 28:4
text: The flood breaketh out from the inhabitant; [even the waters] forgotten of the foot: they are dried up, they are gone away from men.

title: Job 28:5
text: [As for] the earth, out of it cometh bread: and under it is turned up as it were fire.

title: Job 28:6
text: The stones of it [are] the place of sapphires: and it hath dust of gold. {dust...: or, gold ore}

title: Job 28:7
text: [There is] a path which no fowl knoweth, and which the vulture's eye hath not seen:

title: Job 28:8
text: The lion's whelps have not trodden it, nor the fierce lion passed by it.

title: Job 28:9
text: He putteth forth his hand upon the rock; he overturneth the mountains by the roots. {rock: or, flint}

title: Job 28:10
text: He cutteth out rivers among the rocks; and his eye seeth every precious thing.

title: Job 28:11
text: He bindeth the floods from overflowing; and [the thing that is] hid bringeth he forth to light. {overflowing: Heb. weeping}

title: Job 28:12
text: But where shall wisdom be found? and where [is] the place of understanding?

title: Job 28:13
text: Man knoweth not the price thereof; neither is it found in the land of the living.

title: Job 28:14
text: ¶The depth saith, It [is] not in me: and the sea saith, [It is] not with me.

title: Job 28:15
text: It cannot be gotten for gold, neither shall silver be weighed [for] the price thereof. {It...: Heb. Fine gold shall not be given for it}

title: Job 28:16
text: It cannot be valued with the gold of Ophir, with the precious onyx, or the sapphire.

title: Job 28:17
text: The gold and the crystal cannot equal it: and the exchange of it [shall not be for] jewels of fine gold. {jewels...: or, vessels of}

title: Job 28:18
text: No mention shall be made of coral, or of pearls: for the price of wisdom [is] above rubies. {coral: or, Ramoth}

title: Job 28:19
text: The topaz of Ethiopia shall not equal it, neither shall it be valued with pure gold.

title: Job 28:20
text: ¶Whence then cometh wisdom? and where [is] the place of understanding?

title: Job 28:21
text: Seeing it is hid from the eyes of all living, and kept close from the fowls of the air. {air: or, heaven}

title: Job 28:22
text: Destruction and death say, We have heard the fame thereof with our ears.

title: Job 28:23
text: God understandeth the way thereof, and he knoweth the place thereof.

title: Job 28:24
text: For he looketh to the ends of the earth, [and] seeth under the whole heaven;

title: Job 28:25
text: To make the weight for the winds; and he weigheth the waters by measure.

title: Job 28:26
text: When he made a decree for the rain, and a way for the lightning of the thunder:

title: Job 28:27
text: Then did he see it, and declare it; he prepared it, yea, and searched it out. {declare...: or, number it}

title: Job 28:28
text: And unto man he said, Behold, the fear of the Lord, that [is] wisdom; and to depart from evil [is] understanding.

title: Job 29:1
text: ¶Moreover Job continued his parable, and said, {continued: Heb. added to take up}

title: Job 29:2
text: Oh that I were as [in] months past, as [in] the days [when] God preserved me;

title: Job 29:3
text: When his candle shined upon my head, [and when] by his light I walked [through] darkness; {candle: or, lamp}

title: Job 29:4
text: As I was in the days of my youth, when the secret of God [was] upon my tabernacle;

title: Job 29:5
text: When the Almighty [was] yet with me, [when] my children [were] about me;

title: Job 29:6
text: When I washed my steps with butter, and the rock poured me out rivers of oil; {me: Heb. with me}

title: Job 29:7
text: ¶When I went out to the gate through the city, [when] I prepared my seat in the street!

title: Job 29:8
text: The young men saw me, and hid themselves: and the aged arose, [and] stood up.

title: Job 29:9
text: The princes refrained talking, and laid [their] hand on their mouth.

title: Job 29:10
text: The nobles held their peace, and their tongue cleaved to the roof of their mouth. {The nobles...: Heb. The voice of the nobles was hid}

title: Job 29:11
text: When the ear heard [me], then it blessed me; and when the eye saw [me], it gave witness to me:

title: Job 29:12
text: Because I delivered the poor that cried, and the fatherless, and [him that had] none to help him.

title: Job 29:13
text: The blessing of him that was ready to perish came upon me: and I caused the widow's heart to sing for joy.

title: Job 29:14
text: I put on righteousness, and it clothed me: my judgment [was] as a robe and a diadem.

title: Job 29:15
text: I was eyes to the blind, and feet [was] I to the lame.

title: Job 29:16
text: I [was] a father to the poor: and the cause [which] I knew not I searched out.

title: Job 29:17
text: And I brake the jaws of the wicked, and plucked the spoil out of his teeth. {the jaws: Heb. the jawteeth, or, the grinders} {plucked: Heb. cast}

title: Job 29:18
text: ¶Then I said, I shall die in my nest, and I shall multiply [my] days as the sand.

title: Job 29:19
text: My root [was] spread out by the waters, and the dew lay all night upon my branch. {spread...: Heb. opened}

title: Job 29:20
text: My glory [was] fresh in me, and my bow was renewed in my hand. {fresh: Heb. new} {renewed: Heb. changed}

title: Job 29:21
text: Unto me [men] gave ear, and waited, and kept silence at my counsel.

title: Job 29:22
text: After my words they spake not again; and my speech dropped upon them.

title: Job 29:23
text: And they waited for me as for the rain; and they opened their mouth wide [as] for the latter rain.

title: Job 29:24
text: [If] I laughed on them, they believed [it] not; and the light of my countenance they cast not down.

title: Job 29:25
text: I chose out their way, and sat chief, and dwelt as a king in the army, as one [that] comforteth the mourners.

title: Job 30:1
text: ¶But now [they that are] younger than I have me in derision, whose fathers I would have disdained to have set with the dogs of my flock. {younger...: Heb. of fewer days than I}

title: Job 30:2
text: Yea, whereto [might] the strength of their hands [profit] me, in whom old age was perished?

title: Job 30:3
text: For want and famine [they were] solitary; fleeing into the wilderness in former time desolate and waste. {solitary: or, dark as the night} {in...: Heb. yesternight}

title: Job 30:4
text: Who cut up mallows by the bushes, and juniper roots [for] their meat.

title: Job 30:5
text: They were driven forth from among [men], (they cried after them as [after] a thief;)

title: Job 30:6
text: To dwell in the clifts of the valleys, [in] caves of the earth, and [in] the rocks. {caves: Heb. holes}

title: Job 30:7
text: Among the bushes they brayed; under the nettles they were gathered together.

title: Job 30:8
text: [They were] children of fools, yea, children of base men: they were viler than the earth. {base...: Heb. men of no name}

title: Job 30:9
text: And now am I their song, yea, I am their byword.

title: Job 30:10
text: They abhor me, they flee far from me, and spare not to spit in my face. {and...: Heb. and withhold not spittle from}

title: Job 30:11
text: Because he hath loosed my cord, and afflicted me, they have also let loose the bridle before me.

title: Job 30:12
text: Upon [my] right [hand] rise the youth; they push away my feet, and they raise up against me the ways of their destruction.

title: Job 30:13
text: They mar my path, they set forward my calamity, they have no helper.

title: Job 30:14
text: They came [upon me] as a wide breaking in [of waters]: in the desolation they rolled themselves [upon me].

title: Job 30:15
text: ¶Terrors are turned upon me: they pursue my soul as the wind: and my welfare passeth away as a cloud. {my soul: Heb. my principal one}

title: Job 30:16
text: And now my soul is poured out upon me; the days of affliction have taken hold upon me.

title: Job 30:17
text: My bones are pierced in me in the night season: and my sinews take no rest.

title: Job 30:18
text: By the great force [of my disease] is my garment changed: it bindeth me about as the collar of my coat.

title: Job 30:19
text: He hath cast me into the mire, and I am become like dust and ashes.

title: Job 30:20
text: I cry unto thee, and thou dost not hear me: I stand up, and thou regardest me [not].

title: Job 30:21
text: Thou art become cruel to me: with thy strong hand thou opposest thyself against me. {become...: Heb. turned to be cruel} {thy...: Heb. the strength of thy hand}

title: Job 30:22
text: Thou liftest me up to the wind; thou causest me to ride [upon it], and dissolvest my substance. {substance: or, wisdom}

title: Job 30:23
text: For I know [that] thou wilt bring me [to] death, and [to] the house appointed for all living.

title: Job 30:24
text: Howbeit he will not stretch out [his] hand to the grave, though they cry in his destruction. {grave: Heb. heap}

title: Job 30:25
text: Did not I weep for him that was in trouble? was [not] my soul grieved for the poor? {in trouble: Heb. hard of day?}

title: Job 30:26
text: When I looked for good, then evil came [unto me]: and when I waited for light, there came darkness.

title: Job 30:27
text: My bowels boiled, and rested not: the days of affliction prevented me.

title: Job 30:28
text: I went mourning without the sun: I stood up, [and] I cried in the congregation.

title: Job 30:29
text: I am a brother to dragons, and a companion to owls. {owls: or, ostriches}

title: Job 30:30
text: My skin is black upon me, and my bones are burned with heat.

title: Job 30:31
text: My harp also is [turned] to mourning, and my organ into the voice of them that weep.

title: Job 31:1
text: ¶I made a covenant with mine eyes; why then should I think upon a maid?

title: Job 31:2
text: For what portion of God [is there] from above? and [what] inheritance of the Almighty from on high?

title: Job 31:3
text: [Is] not destruction to the wicked? and a strange [punishment] to the workers of iniquity?

title: Job 31:4
text: Doth not he see my ways, and count all my steps?

title: Job 31:5
text: If I have walked with vanity, or if my foot hath hasted to deceit;

title: Job 31:6
text: Let me be weighed in an even balance, that God may know mine integrity. {Let...: Heb. Let him weigh me in balances of justice}

title: Job 31:7
text: If my step hath turned out of the way, and mine heart walked after mine eyes, and if any blot hath cleaved to mine hands;

title: Job 31:8
text: [Then] let me sow, and let another eat; yea, let my offspring be rooted out.

title: Job 31:9
text: ¶If mine heart have been deceived by a woman, or [if] I have laid wait at my neighbour's door;

title: Job 31:10
text: [Then] let my wife grind unto another, and let others bow down upon her.

title: Job 31:11
text: For this [is] an heinous crime; yea, it [is] an iniquity [to be punished by] the judges.

title: Job 31:12
text: For it [is] a fire [that] consumeth to destruction, and would root out all mine increase.

title: Job 31:13
text: If I did despise the cause of my manservant or of my maidservant, when they contended with me;

title: Job 31:14
text: What then shall I do when God riseth up? and when he visiteth, what shall I answer him?

title: Job 31:15
text: Did not he that made me in the womb make him? and did not one fashion us in the womb? {did not one...: or, did he not fashion us in one womb?}

title: Job 31:16
text: ¶If I have withheld the poor from [their] desire, or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail;

title: Job 31:17
text: Or have eaten my morsel myself alone, and the fatherless hath not eaten thereof;

title: Job 31:18
text: (For from my youth he was brought up with me, as [with] a father, and I have guided her from my mother's womb;) {her: that is, the widow}

title: Job 31:19
text: If I have seen any perish for want of clothing, or any poor without covering;

title: Job 31:20
text: If his loins have not blessed me, and [if] he were [not] warmed with the fleece of my sheep;

title: Job 31:21
text: If I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless, when I saw my help in the gate:

title: Job 31:22
text: [Then] let mine arm fall from my shoulder blade, and mine arm be broken from the bone. {bone: or, chanelbone}

title: Job 31:23
text: For destruction [from] God [was] a terror to me, and by reason of his highness I could not endure.

title: Job 31:24
text: ¶If I have made gold my hope, or have said to the fine gold, [Thou art] my confidence;

title: Job 31:25
text: If I rejoiced because my wealth [was] great, and because mine hand had gotten much; {gotten...: Heb. found much}

title: Job 31:26
text: If I beheld the sun when it shined, or the moon walking [in] brightness; {sun: Heb. light} {in...: Heb. bright}

title: Job 31:27
text: And my heart hath been secretly enticed, or my mouth hath kissed my hand: {my mouth...: Heb. my hand hath kissed my mouth}

title: Job 31:28
text: This also [were] an iniquity [to be punished by] the judge: for I should have denied the God [that is] above.

title: Job 31:29
text: If I rejoiced at the destruction of him that hated me, or lifted up myself when evil found him:

title: Job 31:30
text: Neither have I suffered my mouth to sin by wishing a curse to his soul. {mouth: Heb. palate}

title: Job 31:31
text: If the men of my tabernacle said not, Oh that we had of his flesh! we cannot be satisfied.

title: Job 31:32
text: The stranger did not lodge in the street: [but] I opened my doors to the traveller. {traveller: or, way}

title: Job 31:33
text: ¶If I covered my transgressions as Adam, by hiding mine iniquity in my bosom: {as Adam: or, after the manner of men}

title: Job 31:34
text: Did I fear a great multitude, or did the contempt of families terrify me, that I kept silence, [and] went not out of the door?

title: Job 31:35
text: Oh that one would hear me! behold, my desire [is, that] the Almighty would answer me, and [that] mine adversary had written a book. {my...: or, my sign is that the Almighty will}

title: Job 31:36
text: Surely I would take it upon my shoulder, [and] bind it [as] a crown to me.

title: Job 31:37
text: I would declare unto him the number of my steps; as a prince would I go near unto him.

title: Job 31:38
text: If my land cry against me, or that the furrows likewise thereof complain; {complain: Heb. weep}

title: Job 31:39
text: If I have eaten the fruits thereof without money, or have caused the owners thereof to lose their life: {fruits: Heb. strength} {the owners...: Heb. the soul of the owners thereof to expire, or, breathe out}

title: Job 31:40
text: Let thistles grow instead of wheat, and cockle instead of barley. The words of Job are ended. {cockle: or, noisome weeds}

title: Job 32:1
text: ¶So these three men ceased to answer Job, because he [was] righteous in his own eyes. {to...: Heb. from answering}

title: Job 32:2
text: Then was kindled the wrath of Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the kindred of Ram: against Job was his wrath kindled, because he justified himself rather than God. {himself: Heb. his soul}

title: Job 32:3
text: Also against his three friends was his wrath kindled, because they had found no answer, and [yet] had condemned Job.

title: Job 32:4
text: Now Elihu had waited till Job had spoken, because they [were] elder than he. {waited...: Heb. expected Job in words} {elder: Heb. elder for days}

title: Job 32:5
text: When Elihu saw that [there was] no answer in the mouth of [these] three men, then his wrath was kindled.

title: Job 32:6
text: ¶And Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite answered and said, I [am] young, and ye [are] very old; wherefore I was afraid, and durst not shew you mine opinion. {young: Heb. few of days} {durst...: Heb. feared}

title: Job 32:7
text: I said, Days should speak, and multitude of years should teach wisdom.

title: Job 32:8
text: But [there is] a spirit in man: and the inspiration of the Almighty giveth them understanding.

title: Job 32:9
text: Great men are not [always] wise: neither do the aged understand judgment.

title: Job 32:10
text: Therefore I said, Hearken to me; I also will shew mine opinion.

title: Job 32:11
text: Behold, I waited for your words; I gave ear to your reasons, whilst ye searched out what to say. {reasons: Heb. understandings} {what...: Heb. words}

title: Job 32:12
text: Yea, I attended unto you, and, behold, [there was] none of you that convinced Job, [or] that answered his words:

title: Job 32:13
text: Lest ye should say, We have found out wisdom: God thrusteth him down, not man.

title: Job 32:14
text: Now he hath not directed [his] words against me: neither will I answer him with your speeches. {directed: or, ordered}

title: Job 32:15
text: ¶They were amazed, they answered no more: they left off speaking. {left...: Heb. removed speeches from themselves}

title: Job 32:16
text: When I had waited, (for they spake not, but stood still, [and] answered no more;)

title: Job 32:17
text: [I said], I will answer also my part, I also will shew mine opinion.

title: Job 32:18
text: For I am full of matter, the spirit within me constraineth me. {matter: Heb. words} {spirit...: Heb. spirit of my belly}

title: Job 32:19
text: Behold, my belly [is] as wine [which] hath no vent; it is ready to burst like new bottles. {hath...: Heb. is not opened}

title: Job 32:20
text: I will speak, that I may be refreshed: I will open my lips and answer. {be...: Heb. breathe}

title: Job 32:21
text: Let me not, I pray you, accept any man's person, neither let me give flattering titles unto man.

title: Job 32:22
text: For I know not to give flattering titles; [in so doing] my maker would soon take me away.

title: Job 33:1
text: ¶Wherefore, Job, I pray thee, hear my speeches, and hearken to all my words.

title: Job 33:2
text: Behold, now I have opened my mouth, my tongue hath spoken in my mouth. {in my mouth: Heb. in my palate}

title: Job 33:3
text: My words [shall be of] the uprightness of my heart: and my lips shall utter knowledge clearly.

title: Job 33:4
text: The Spirit of God hath made me, and the breath of the Almighty hath given me life.

title: Job 33:5
text: If thou canst answer me, set [thy words] in order before me, stand up.

title: Job 33:6
text: Behold, I [am] according to thy wish in God's stead: I also am formed out of the clay. {wish: Heb. mouth} {formed: Heb. cut}

title: Job 33:7
text: Behold, my terror shall not make thee afraid, neither shall my hand be heavy upon thee.

title: Job 33:8
text: ¶Surely thou hast spoken in mine hearing, and I have heard the voice of [thy] words, [saying], {hearing: Heb. ears}

title: Job 33:9
text: I am clean without transgression, I [am] innocent; neither [is there] iniquity in me.

title: Job 33:10
text: Behold, he findeth occasions against me, he counteth me for his enemy,

title: Job 33:11
text: He putteth my feet in the stocks, he marketh all my paths.

title: Job 33:12
text: Behold, [in] this thou art not just: I will answer thee, that God is greater than man.

title: Job 33:13
text: Why dost thou strive against him? for he giveth not account of any of his matters. {he giveth...: Heb. he answereth not}

title: Job 33:14
text: ¶For God speaketh once, yea twice, [yet man] perceiveth it not.

title: Job 33:15
text: In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falleth upon men, in slumberings upon the bed;

title: Job 33:16
text: Then he openeth the ears of men, and sealeth their instruction, {he...: Heb. he revealeth, or, uncovereth}

title: Job 33:17
text: That he may withdraw man [from his] purpose, and hide pride from man. {purpose: Heb. work}

title: Job 33:18
text: He keepeth back his soul from the pit, and his life from perishing by the sword. {from perishing: Heb. from passing}

title: Job 33:19
text: ¶He is chastened also with pain upon his bed, and the multitude of his bones with strong [pain]:

title: Job 33:20
text: So that his life abhorreth bread, and his soul dainty meat. {dainty...: Heb. meat of desire}

title: Job 33:21
text: His flesh is consumed away, that it cannot be seen; and his bones [that] were not seen stick out.

title: Job 33:22
text: Yea, his soul draweth near unto the grave, and his life to the destroyers.

title: Job 33:23
text: If there be a messenger with him, an interpreter, one among a thousand, to shew unto man his uprightness:

title: Job 33:24
text: Then he is gracious unto him, and saith, Deliver him from going down to the pit: I have found a ransom. {a ransom: or, an atonement}

title: Job 33:25
text: His flesh shall be fresher than a child's: he shall return to the days of his youth: {a child's: Heb. childhood}

title: Job 33:26
text: He shall pray unto God, and he will be favourable unto him: and he shall see his face with joy: for he will render unto man his righteousness.

title: Job 33:27
text: He looketh upon men, and [if any] say, I have sinned, and perverted [that which was] right, and it profited me not; {He...: or, He shall look upon men, and say}

title: Job 33:28
text: He will deliver his soul from going into the pit, and his life shall see the light. {He...: or, He hath delivered my soul, etc, and my life}

title: Job 33:29
text: ¶Lo, all these [things] worketh God oftentimes with man, {oftentimes: Heb. twice and thrice}

title: Job 33:30
text: To bring back his soul from the pit, to be enlightened with the light of the living.

title: Job 33:31
text: Mark well, O Job, hearken unto me: hold thy peace, and I will speak.

title: Job 33:32
text: If thou hast any thing to say, answer me: speak, for I desire to justify thee.

title: Job 33:33
text: If not, hearken unto me: hold thy peace, and I shall teach thee wisdom.

title: Job 34:1
text: ¶Furthermore Elihu answered and said,

title: Job 34:2
text: Hear my words, O ye wise [men]; and give ear unto me, ye that have knowledge.

title: Job 34:3
text: For the ear trieth words, as the mouth tasteth meat. {mouth: Heb. palate}

title: Job 34:4
text: Let us choose to us judgment: let us know among ourselves what [is] good.

title: Job 34:5
text: For Job hath said, I am righteous: and God hath taken away my judgment.

title: Job 34:6
text: Should I lie against my right? my wound [is] incurable without transgression. {my wound: Heb. mine arrow}

title: Job 34:7
text: What man [is] like Job, [who] drinketh up scorning like water?

title: Job 34:8
text: Which goeth in company with the workers of iniquity, and walketh with wicked men.

title: Job 34:9
text: For he hath said, It profiteth a man nothing that he should delight himself with God.

title: Job 34:10
text: ¶Therefore hearken unto me, ye men of understanding: far be it from God, [that he should do] wickedness; and [from] the Almighty, [that he should commit] iniquity. {men...: Heb. men of heart}

title: Job 34:11
text: For the work of a man shall he render unto him, and cause every man to find according to [his] ways.

title: Job 34:12
text: Yea, surely God will not do wickedly, neither will the Almighty pervert judgment.

title: Job 34:13
text: Who hath given him a charge over the earth? or who hath disposed the whole world? {the whole: Heb. all of it?}

title: Job 34:14
text: If he set his heart upon man, [if] he gather unto himself his spirit and his breath; {man: Heb. him}

title: Job 34:15
text: All flesh shall perish together, and man shall turn again unto dust.

title: Job 34:16
text: ¶If now [thou hast] understanding, hear this: hearken to the voice of my words.

title: Job 34:17
text: Shall even he that hateth right govern? and wilt thou condemn him that is most just? {govern: Heb. bind?}

title: Job 34:18
text: [Is it fit] to say to a king, [Thou art] wicked? [and] to princes, [Ye are] ungodly?

title: Job 34:19
text: [How much less to him] that accepteth not the persons of princes, nor regardeth the rich more than the poor? for they all [are] the work of his hands.

title: Job 34:20
text: In a moment shall they die, and the people shall be troubled at midnight, and pass away: and the mighty shall be taken away without hand. {the mighty...: Heb. they shall take away the mighty}

title: Job 34:21
text: For his eyes [are] upon the ways of man, and he seeth all his goings.

title: Job 34:22
text: [There is] no darkness, nor shadow of death, where the workers of iniquity may hide themselves.

title: Job 34:23
text: For he will not lay upon man more [than right]; that he should enter into judgment with God. {enter: Heb. go}

title: Job 34:24
text: He shall break in pieces mighty men without number, and set others in their stead. {number: Heb. searching out}

title: Job 34:25
text: Therefore he knoweth their works, and he overturneth [them] in the night, so that they are destroyed. {destroyed: Heb. crushed}

title: Job 34:26
text: He striketh them as wicked men in the open sight of others; {open...: Heb. place of beholders}

title: Job 34:27
text: Because they turned back from him, and would not consider any of his ways: {him: Heb. after him}

title: Job 34:28
text: So that they cause the cry of the poor to come unto him, and he heareth the cry of the afflicted.

title: Job 34:29
text: When he giveth quietness, who then can make trouble? and when he hideth [his] face, who then can behold him? whether [it be done] against a nation, or against a man only:

title: Job 34:30
text: That the hypocrite reign not, lest the people be ensnared.

title: Job 34:31
text: ¶Surely it is meet to be said unto God, I have borne [chastisement], I will not offend [any more]:

title: Job 34:32
text: [That which] I see not teach thou me: if I have done iniquity, I will do no more.

title: Job 34:33
text: [Should it be] according to thy mind? he will recompense it, whether thou refuse, or whether thou choose; and not I: therefore speak what thou knowest. {according...: Heb. from with thee?}

title: Job 34:34
text: Let men of understanding tell me, and let a wise man hearken unto me. {of...: Heb. of heart}

title: Job 34:35
text: Job hath spoken without knowledge, and his words [were] without wisdom.

title: Job 34:36
text: My desire [is that] Job may be tried unto the end because of [his] answers for wicked men. {My...: or, My father, let Job be tried}

title: Job 34:37
text: For he addeth rebellion unto his sin, he clappeth [his hands] among us, and multiplieth his words against God.

title: Job 35:1
text: ¶Elihu spake moreover, and said,

title: Job 35:2
text: Thinkest thou this to be right, [that] thou saidst, My righteousness [is] more than God's?

title: Job 35:3
text: For thou saidst, What advantage will it be unto thee? [and], What profit shall I have, [if I be cleansed] from my sin? {if...: or, by it more than by my sin}

title: Job 35:4
text: I will answer thee, and thy companions with thee. {answer...: Heb. return to thee words}

title: Job 35:5
text: Look unto the heavens, and see; and behold the clouds [which] are higher than thou.

title: Job 35:6
text: If thou sinnest, what doest thou against him? or [if] thy transgressions be multiplied, what doest thou unto him?

title: Job 35:7
text: If thou be righteous, what givest thou him? or what receiveth he of thine hand?

title: Job 35:8
text: Thy wickedness [may hurt] a man as thou [art]; and thy righteousness [may profit] the son of man.

title: Job 35:9
text: ¶By reason of the multitude of oppressions they make [the oppressed] to cry: they cry out by reason of the arm of the mighty.

title: Job 35:10
text: But none saith, Where [is] God my maker, who giveth songs in the night;

title: Job 35:11
text: Who teacheth us more than the beasts of the earth, and maketh us wiser than the fowls of heaven?

title: Job 35:12
text: There they cry, but none giveth answer, because of the pride of evil men.

title: Job 35:13
text: Surely God will not hear vanity, neither will the Almighty regard it.

title: Job 35:14
text: ¶Although thou sayest thou shalt not see him, [yet] judgment [is] before him; therefore trust thou in him.

title: Job 35:15
text: But now, because [it is] not [so], he hath visited in his anger; yet he knoweth [it] not in great extremity: {he hath: that is, God hath} {he knoweth: that is, Job knoweth}

title: Job 35:16
text: Therefore doth Job open his mouth in vain; he multiplieth words without knowledge.

title: Job 36:1
text: ¶Elihu also proceeded, and said,

title: Job 36:2
text: Suffer me a little, and I will shew thee that [I have] yet to speak on God's behalf. {I have...: Heb. there are yet words for God}

title: Job 36:3
text: I will fetch my knowledge from afar, and will ascribe righteousness to my Maker.

title: Job 36:4
text: For truly my words [shall] not [be] false: he that is perfect in knowledge [is] with thee.

title: Job 36:5
text: ¶Behold, God [is] mighty, and despiseth not [any: he is] mighty in strength [and] wisdom. {wisdom: Heb. heart}

title: Job 36:6
text: He preserveth not the life of the wicked: but giveth right to the poor. {poor: or, afflicted}

title: Job 36:7
text: He withdraweth not his eyes from the righteous: but with kings [are they] on the throne; yea, he doth establish them for ever, and they are exalted.

title: Job 36:8
text: And if [they be] bound in fetters, [and] be holden in cords of affliction;

title: Job 36:9
text: Then he sheweth them their work, and their transgressions that they have exceeded.

title: Job 36:10
text: He openeth also their ear to discipline, and commandeth that they return from iniquity.

title: Job 36:11
text: If they obey and serve [him], they shall spend their days in prosperity, and their years in pleasures.

title: Job 36:12
text: But if they obey not, they shall perish by the sword, and they shall die without knowledge. {perish: Heb. pass away}

title: Job 36:13
text: But the hypocrites in heart heap up wrath: they cry not when he bindeth them.

title: Job 36:14
text: They die in youth, and their life [is] among the unclean. {They...: Heb. Their soul dieth} {unclean: or, sodomites}

title: Job 36:15
text: ¶He delivereth the poor in his affliction, and openeth their ears in oppression. {poor: or, afflicted}

title: Job 36:16
text: Even so would he have removed thee out of the strait [into] a broad place, where [there is] no straitness; and that which should be set on thy table [should be] full of fatness. {that...: Heb. the rest of thy table}

title: Job 36:17
text: But thou hast fulfilled the judgment of the wicked: judgment and justice take hold [on thee]. {take...: or, should uphold thee}

title: Job 36:18
text: Because [there is] wrath, [beware] lest he take thee away with [his] stroke: then a great ransom cannot deliver thee. {deliver...: Heb. turn thee aside}

title: Job 36:19
text: Will he esteem thy riches? [no], not gold, nor all the forces of strength.

title: Job 36:20
text: Desire not the night, when people are cut off in their place.

title: Job 36:21
text: Take heed, regard not iniquity: for this hast thou chosen rather than affliction.

title: Job 36:22
text: Behold, God exalteth by his power: who teacheth like him?

title: Job 36:23
text: Who hath enjoined him his way? or who can say, Thou hast wrought iniquity?

title: Job 36:24
text: ¶Remember that thou magnify his work, which men behold.

title: Job 36:25
text: Every man may see it; man may behold [it] afar off.

title: Job 36:26
text: Behold, God [is] great, and we know [him] not, neither can the number of his years be searched out.

title: Job 36:27
text: For he maketh small the drops of water: they pour down rain according to the vapour thereof:

title: Job 36:28
text: Which the clouds do drop [and] distil upon man abundantly.

title: Job 36:29
text: Also can [any] understand the spreadings of the clouds, [or] the noise of his tabernacle?

title: Job 36:30
text: Behold, he spreadeth his light upon it, and covereth the bottom of the sea. {bottom: Heb. roots}

title: Job 36:31
text: For by them judgeth he the people; he giveth meat in abundance.

title: Job 36:32
text: With clouds he covereth the light; and commandeth it [not to shine] by [the cloud] that cometh betwixt.

title: Job 36:33
text: The noise thereof sheweth concerning it, the cattle also concerning the vapour. {the vapour: Heb. that which goeth up}

title: Job 37:1
text: ¶At this also my heart trembleth, and is moved out of his place.

title: Job 37:2
text: Hear attentively the noise of his voice, and the sound [that] goeth out of his mouth. {Hear...: Heb. Hear in hearing}

title: Job 37:3
text: He directeth it under the whole heaven, and his lightning unto the ends of the earth. {lightning: Heb. light} {ends: Heb. wings}

title: Job 37:4
text: After it a voice roareth: he thundereth with the voice of his excellency; and he will not stay them when his voice is heard.

title: Job 37:5
text: God thundereth marvellously with his voice; great things doeth he, which we cannot comprehend.

title: Job 37:6
text: ¶For he saith to the snow, Be thou [on] the earth; likewise to the small rain, and to the great rain of his strength. {likewise...: Heb. and to the shower of rain, and to the showers of rain of his strength}

title: Job 37:7
text: He sealeth up the hand of every man; that all men may know his work.

title: Job 37:8
text: Then the beasts go into dens, and remain in their places.

title: Job 37:9
text: Out of the south cometh the whirlwind: and cold out of the north. {south: Heb. chamber} {north: Heb. scattering winds}

title: Job 37:10
text: By the breath of God frost is given: and the breadth of the waters is straitened.

title: Job 37:11
text: Also by watering he wearieth the thick cloud: he scattereth his bright cloud: {his...: Heb. the cloud of his light}

title: Job 37:12
text: And it is turned round about by his counsels: that they may do whatsoever he commandeth them upon the face of the world in the earth.

title: Job 37:13
text: He causeth it to come, whether for correction, or for his land, or for mercy. {correction: Heb. a rod}

title: Job 37:14
text: ¶Hearken unto this, O Job: stand still, and consider the wondrous works of God.

title: Job 37:15
text: Dost thou know when God disposed them, and caused the light of his cloud to shine?

title: Job 37:16
text: Dost thou know the balancings of the clouds, the wondrous works of him which is perfect in knowledge?

title: Job 37:17
text: How thy garments [are] warm, when he quieteth the earth by the south [wind]?

title: Job 37:18
text: Hast thou with him spread out the sky, [which is] strong, [and] as a molten looking glass?

title: Job 37:19
text: Teach us what we shall say unto him; [for] we cannot order [our speech] by reason of darkness.

title: Job 37:20
text: Shall it be told him that I speak? if a man speak, surely he shall be swallowed up.

title: Job 37:21
text: ¶And now [men] see not the bright light which [is] in the clouds: but the wind passeth, and cleanseth them.

title: Job 37:22
text: Fair weather cometh out of the north: with God [is] terrible majesty. {Fair...: Heb. Gold}

title: Job 37:23
text: [Touching] the Almighty, we cannot find him out: [he is] excellent in power, and in judgment, and in plenty of justice: he will not afflict.

title: Job 37:24
text: Men do therefore fear him: he respecteth not any [that are] wise of heart.

title: Job 38:1
text: ¶Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind, and said,

title: Job 38:2
text: Who [is] this that darkeneth counsel by words without knowledge?

title: Job 38:3
text: Gird up now thy loins like a man; for I will demand of thee, and answer thou me. {answer...: Heb. make me know}

title: Job 38:4
text: ¶Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? declare, if thou hast understanding. {hast...: Heb. knowest understanding}

title: Job 38:5
text: Who hath laid the measures thereof, if thou knowest? or who hath stretched the line upon it?

title: Job 38:6
text: Whereupon are the foundations thereof fastened? or who laid the corner stone thereof; {foundations: Heb. sockets} {fastened: Heb. made to sink?}

title: Job 38:7
text: When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?

title: Job 38:8
text: Or [who] shut up the sea with doors, when it brake forth, [as if] it had issued out of the womb?

title: Job 38:9
text: When I made the cloud the garment thereof, and thick darkness a swaddlingband for it,

title: Job 38:10
text: And brake up for it my decreed [place], and set bars and doors, {brake...: or, established my decree upon it}

title: Job 38:11
text: And said, Hitherto shalt thou come, but no further: and here shall thy proud waves be stayed? {thy...: Heb. the pride of thy waves}

title: Job 38:12
text: ¶Hast thou commanded the morning since thy days; [and] caused the dayspring to know his place;

title: Job 38:13
text: That it might take hold of the ends of the earth, that the wicked might be shaken out of it? {ends: Heb. wings}

title: Job 38:14
text: It is turned as clay [to] the seal; and they stand as a garment.

title: Job 38:15
text: And from the wicked their light is withholden, and the high arm shall be broken.

title: Job 38:16
text: Hast thou entered into the springs of the sea? or hast thou walked in the search of the depth?

title: Job 38:17
text: Have the gates of death been opened unto thee? or hast thou seen the doors of the shadow of death?

title: Job 38:18
text: Hast thou perceived the breadth of the earth? declare if thou knowest it all.

title: Job 38:19
text: Where [is] the way [where] light dwelleth? and [as for] darkness, where [is] the place thereof,

title: Job 38:20
text: That thou shouldest take it to the bound thereof, and that thou shouldest know the paths [to] the house thereof? {to the bound: or, at, etc}

title: Job 38:21
text: Knowest thou [it], because thou wast then born? or [because] the number of thy days [is] great?

title: Job 38:22
text: Hast thou entered into the treasures of the snow? or hast thou seen the treasures of the hail,

title: Job 38:23
text: Which I have reserved against the time of trouble, against the day of battle and war?

title: Job 38:24
text: By what way is the light parted, [which] scattereth the east wind upon the earth?

title: Job 38:25
text: ¶Who hath divided a watercourse for the overflowing of waters, or a way for the lightning of thunder;

title: Job 38:26
text: To cause it to rain on the earth, [where] no man [is; on] the wilderness, wherein [there is] no man;

title: Job 38:27
text: To satisfy the desolate and waste [ground]; and to cause the bud of the tender herb to spring forth?

title: Job 38:28
text: Hath the rain a father? or who hath begotten the drops of dew?

title: Job 38:29
text: Out of whose womb came the ice? and the hoary frost of heaven, who hath gendered it?

title: Job 38:30
text: The waters are hid as [with] a stone, and the face of the deep is frozen. {is...: Heb. is taken}

title: Job 38:31
text: Canst thou bind the sweet influences of Pleiades, or loose the bands of Orion? {Pleiades: or, the seven stars: Heb. Cimah} {Orion: Heb. Cesil?}

title: Job 38:32
text: Canst thou bring forth Mazzaroth in his season? or canst thou guide Arcturus with his sons? {Mazzaroth: or, the twelve signs} {guide: Heb. guide them}

title: Job 38:33
text: Knowest thou the ordinances of heaven? canst thou set the dominion thereof in the earth?

title: Job 38:34
text: Canst thou lift up thy voice to the clouds, that abundance of waters may cover thee?

title: Job 38:35
text: Canst thou send lightnings, that they may go, and say unto thee, Here we [are]? {Here...: Heb. Behold us?}

title: Job 38:36
text: Who hath put wisdom in the inward parts? or who hath given understanding to the heart?

title: Job 38:37
text: Who can number the clouds in wisdom? or who can stay the bottles of heaven, {stay: Heb. cause to lie down}

title: Job 38:38
text: When the dust groweth into hardness, and the clods cleave fast together? {groweth...: or, is turned into mire: Heb. is poured}

title: Job 38:39
text: Wilt thou hunt the prey for the lion? or fill the appetite of the young lions, {the appetite: Heb. the life}

title: Job 38:40
text: When they couch in [their] dens, [and] abide in the covert to lie in wait?

title: Job 38:41
text: Who provideth for the raven his food? when his young ones cry unto God, they wander for lack of meat.

title: Job 39:1
text: ¶Knowest thou the time when the wild goats of the rock bring forth? [or] canst thou mark when the hinds do calve?

title: Job 39:2
text: Canst thou number the months [that] they fulfil? or knowest thou the time when they bring forth?

title: Job 39:3
text: They bow themselves, they bring forth their young ones, they cast out their sorrows.

title: Job 39:4
text: Their young ones are in good liking, they grow up with corn; they go forth, and return not unto them.

title: Job 39:5
text: Who hath sent out the wild ass free? or who hath loosed the bands of the wild ass?

title: Job 39:6
text: Whose house I have made the wilderness, and the barren land his dwellings. {barren...: Heb. salt places}

title: Job 39:7
text: He scorneth the multitude of the city, neither regardeth he the crying of the driver. {of the driver: Heb. of the exactor}

title: Job 39:8
text: The range of the mountains [is] his pasture, and he searcheth after every green thing.

title: Job 39:9
text: Will the unicorn be willing to serve thee, or abide by thy crib?

title: Job 39:10
text: Canst thou bind the unicorn with his band in the furrow? or will he harrow the valleys after thee?

title: Job 39:11
text: Wilt thou trust him, because his strength [is] great? or wilt thou leave thy labour to him?

title: Job 39:12
text: Wilt thou believe him, that he will bring home thy seed, and gather [it into] thy barn?

title: Job 39:13
text: ¶[Gavest thou] the goodly wings unto the peacocks? or wings and feathers unto the ostrich? {wings and...: or, the feathers of the stork and ostrich}

title: Job 39:14
text: Which leaveth her eggs in the earth, and warmeth them in dust,

title: Job 39:15
text: And forgetteth that the foot may crush them, or that the wild beast may break them.

title: Job 39:16
text: She is hardened against her young ones, as though [they were] not hers: her labour is in vain without fear;

title: Job 39:17
text: Because God hath deprived her of wisdom, neither hath he imparted to her understanding.

title: Job 39:18
text: What time she lifteth up herself on high, she scorneth the horse and his rider.

title: Job 39:19
text: ¶Hast thou given the horse strength? hast thou clothed his neck with thunder?

title: Job 39:20
text: Canst thou make him afraid as a grasshopper? the glory of his nostrils [is] terrible. {terrible: Heb. terror}

title: Job 39:21
text: He paweth in the valley, and rejoiceth in [his] strength: he goeth on to meet the armed men. {He paweth: or, His feet dig} {the armed...: Heb. the armour}

title: Job 39:22
text: He mocketh at fear, and is not affrighted; neither turneth he back from the sword.

title: Job 39:23
text: The quiver rattleth against him, the glittering spear and the shield.

title: Job 39:24
text: He swalloweth the ground with fierceness and rage: neither believeth he that [it is] the sound of the trumpet.

title: Job 39:25
text: He saith among the trumpets, Ha, ha; and he smelleth the battle afar off, the thunder of the captains, and the shouting.

title: Job 39:26
text: ¶Doth the hawk fly by thy wisdom, [and] stretch her wings toward the south?

title: Job 39:27
text: Doth the eagle mount up at thy command, and make her nest on high? {at...: Heb. by thy mouth}

title: Job 39:28
text: She dwelleth and abideth on the rock, upon the crag of the rock, and the strong place.

title: Job 39:29
text: From thence she seeketh the prey, [and] her eyes behold afar off.

title: Job 39:30
text: Her young ones also suck up blood: and where the slain [are], there [is] she.

title: Job 40:1
text: ¶Moreover the LORD answered Job, and said,

title: Job 40:2
text: Shall he that contendeth with the Almighty instruct [him]? he that reproveth God, let him answer it.

title: Job 40:3
text: Then Job answered the LORD, and said,

title: Job 40:4
text: Behold, I am vile; what shall I answer thee? I will lay mine hand upon my mouth.

title: Job 40:5
text: Once have I spoken; but I will not answer: yea, twice; but I will proceed no further.

title: Job 40:6
text: ¶Then answered the LORD unto Job out of the whirlwind, and said,

title: Job 40:7
text: Gird up thy loins now like a man: I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto me.

title: Job 40:8
text: Wilt thou also disannul my judgment? wilt thou condemn me, that thou mayest be righteous?

title: Job 40:9
text: Hast thou an arm like God? or canst thou thunder with a voice like him?

title: Job 40:10
text: Deck thyself now [with] majesty and excellency; and array thyself with glory and beauty.

title: Job 40:11
text: Cast abroad the rage of thy wrath: and behold every one [that is] proud, and abase him.

title: Job 40:12
text: Look on every one [that is] proud, [and] bring him low; and tread down the wicked in their place.

title: Job 40:13
text: Hide them in the dust together; [and] bind their faces in secret.

title: Job 40:14
text: Then will I also confess unto thee that thine own right hand can save thee.

title: Job 40:15
text: ¶Behold now behemoth, which I made with thee; he eateth grass as an ox. {behemoth: probably an extinct animal of some kind}

title: Job 40:16
text: Lo now, his strength [is] in his loins, and his force [is] in the navel of his belly.

title: Job 40:17
text: He moveth his tail like a cedar: the sinews of his stones are wrapped together. {He...: or, He setteth up}

title: Job 40:18
text: His bones [are as] strong pieces of brass; his bones [are] like bars of iron.

title: Job 40:19
text: He [is] the chief of the ways of God: he that made him can make his sword to approach [unto him].

title: Job 40:20
text: Surely the mountains bring him forth food, where all the beasts of the field play.

title: Job 40:21
text: He lieth under the shady trees, in the covert of the reed, and fens.

title: Job 40:22
text: The shady trees cover him [with] their shadow; the willows of the brook compass him about.

title: Job 40:23
text: Behold, he drinketh up a river, [and] hasteth not: he trusteth that he can draw up Jordan into his mouth. {he drinketh up: Heb. he oppresseth}

title: Job 40:24
text: He taketh it with his eyes: [his] nose pierceth through snares. {He...: or, Will any take him in his sight, or, bore his nose with a gin?}

title: Job 41:1
text: ¶Canst thou draw out leviathan with an hook? or his tongue with a cord [which] thou lettest down? {leviathan: probably an extinct animal of some kind} {which...: Heb. which thou drownest?}

title: Job 41:2
text: Canst thou put an hook into his nose? or bore his jaw through with a thorn?

title: Job 41:3
text: Will he make many supplications unto thee? will he speak soft [words] unto thee?

title: Job 41:4
text: Will he make a covenant with thee? wilt thou take him for a servant for ever?

title: Job 41:5
text: Wilt thou play with him as [with] a bird? or wilt thou bind him for thy maidens?

title: Job 41:6
text: Shall the companions make a banquet of him? shall they part him among the merchants?

title: Job 41:7
text: Canst thou fill his skin with barbed irons? or his head with fish spears?

title: Job 41:8
text: Lay thine hand upon him, remember the battle, do no more.

title: Job 41:9
text: Behold, the hope of him is in vain: shall not [one] be cast down even at the sight of him?

title: Job 41:10
text: None [is so] fierce that dare stir him up: who then is able to stand before me?

title: Job 41:11
text: ¶Who hath prevented me, that I should repay [him? whatsoever is] under the whole heaven is mine.

title: Job 41:12
text: I will not conceal his parts, nor his power, nor his comely proportion.

title: Job 41:13
text: Who can discover the face of his garment? [or] who can come [to him] with his double bridle? {with: or, within}

title: Job 41:14
text: Who can open the doors of his face? his teeth [are] terrible round about.

title: Job 41:15
text: [His] scales [are his] pride, shut up together [as with] a close seal. {scales: Heb. strong pieces of shields}

title: Job 41:16
text: One is so near to another, that no air can come between them.

title: Job 41:17
text: They are joined one to another, they stick together, that they cannot be sundered.

title: Job 41:18
text: By his neesings a light doth shine, and his eyes [are] like the eyelids of the morning.

title: Job 41:19
text: Out of his mouth go burning lamps, [and] sparks of fire leap out.

title: Job 41:20
text: Out of his nostrils goeth smoke, as [out] of a seething pot or caldron.

title: Job 41:21
text: His breath kindleth coals, and a flame goeth out of his mouth.

title: Job 41:22
text: In his neck remaineth strength, and sorrow is turned into joy before him. {is turned into joy: Heb. rejoiceth}

title: Job 41:23
text: The flakes of his flesh are joined together: they are firm in themselves; they cannot be moved. {flakes: Heb. fallings}

title: Job 41:24
text: His heart is as firm as a stone; yea, as hard as a piece of the nether [millstone].

title: Job 41:25
text: When he raiseth up himself, the mighty are afraid: by reason of breakings they purify themselves.

title: Job 41:26
text: The sword of him that layeth at him cannot hold: the spear, the dart, nor the habergeon. {habergeon: or, breastplate}

title: Job 41:27
text: He esteemeth iron as straw, [and] brass as rotten wood.

title: Job 41:28
text: The arrow cannot make him flee: slingstones are turned with him into stubble.

title: Job 41:29
text: Darts are counted as stubble: he laugheth at the shaking of a spear.

title: Job 41:30
text: Sharp stones [are] under him: he spreadeth sharp pointed things upon the mire. {Sharp stones: Heb. Sharp pieces of potsherd}

title: Job 41:31
text: He maketh the deep to boil like a pot: he maketh the sea like a pot of ointment.

title: Job 41:32
text: He maketh a path to shine after him; [one] would think the deep [to be] hoary.

title: Job 41:33
text: Upon earth there is not his like, who is made without fear. {is made without fear: or, behave themselves without fear}

title: Job 41:34
text: He beholdeth all high [things]: he [is] a king over all the children of pride.

title: Job 42:1
text: ¶Then Job answered the LORD, and said,

title: Job 42:2
text: I know that thou canst do every [thing], and [that] no thought can be withholden from thee. {no thought can be...: or, no thought of thine can be hindered}

title: Job 42:3
text: Who [is] he that hideth counsel without knowledge? therefore have I uttered that I understood not; things too wonderful for me, which I knew not.

title: Job 42:4
text: Hear, I beseech thee, and I will speak: I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto me.

title: Job 42:5
text: I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine eye seeth thee.

title: Job 42:6
text: Wherefore I abhor [myself], and repent in dust and ashes.

title: Job 42:7
text: ¶And it was [so], that after the LORD had spoken these words unto Job, the LORD said to Eliphaz the Temanite, My wrath is kindled against thee, and against thy two friends: for ye have not spoken of me [the thing that is] right, as my servant Job [hath].

title: Job 42:8
text: Therefore take unto you now seven bullocks and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt offering; and my servant Job shall pray for you: for him will I accept: lest I deal with you [after your] folly, in that ye have not spoken of me [the thing which is] right, like my servant Job. {him: Heb. his face, or, person}

title: Job 42:9
text: So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite [and] Zophar the Naamathite went, and did according as the LORD commanded them: the LORD also accepted Job. {Job: Heb. the face of Job}

title: Job 42:10
text: ¶And the LORD turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends: also the LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before. {gave...: Heb. added all that had been to Job unto the double}

title: Job 42:11
text: Then came there unto him all his brethren, and all his sisters, and all they that had been of his acquaintance before, and did eat bread with him in his house: and they bemoaned him, and comforted him over all the evil that the LORD had brought upon him: every man also gave him a piece of money, and every one an earring of gold.

title: Job 42:12
text: So the LORD blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning: for he had fourteen thousand sheep, and six thousand camels, and a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand she asses.

title: Job 42:13
text: He had also seven sons and three daughters.

title: Job 42:14
text: And he called the name of the first, Jemima; and the name of the second, Kezia; and the name of the third, Kerenhappuch.

title: Job 42:15
text: And in all the land were no women found [so] fair as the daughters of Job: and their father gave them inheritance among their brethren.

title: Job 42:16
text: After this lived Job an hundred and forty years, and saw his sons, and his sons' sons, [even] four generations.

title: Job 42:17
text: So Job died, [being] old and full of days.

title: Psalms 1:1
text: ¶Blessed [is] the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful. {ungodly: or, wicked}

title: Psalms 1:2
text: But his delight [is] in the law of the LORD; and in his law doth he meditate day and night.

title: Psalms 1:3
text: And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither; and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper. {wither: Heb. fade}

title: Psalms 1:4
text: ¶The ungodly [are] not so: but [are] like the chaff which the wind driveth away.

title: Psalms 1:5
text: Therefore the ungodly shall not stand in the judgment, nor sinners in the congregation of the righteous.

title: Psalms 1:6
text: For the LORD knoweth the way of the righteous: but the way of the ungodly shall perish.

title: Psalms 2:1
text: ¶Why do the heathen rage, and the people imagine a vain thing? {rage: or, tumultuously assemble} {imagine: Heb. meditate}

title: Psalms 2:2
text: The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together, against the LORD, and against his anointed, [saying],

title: Psalms 2:3
text: Let us break their bands asunder, and cast away their cords from us.

title: Psalms 2:4
text: He that sitteth in the heavens shall laugh: the Lord shall have them in derision.

title: Psalms 2:5
text: Then shall he speak unto them in his wrath, and vex them in his sore displeasure. {vex: or, trouble}

title: Psalms 2:6
text: Yet have I set my king upon my holy hill of Zion. {set: Heb. anointed} {upon...: Heb. upon Zion, the hill of my holiness}

title: Psalms 2:7
text: ¶I will declare the decree: the LORD hath said unto me, Thou [art] my Son; this day have I begotten thee. {the decree: or, for a decree}

title: Psalms 2:8
text: Ask of me, and I shall give [thee] the heathen [for] thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth [for] thy possession.

title: Psalms 2:9
text: Thou shalt break them with a rod of iron; thou shalt dash them in pieces like a potter's vessel.

title: Psalms 2:10
text: ¶Be wise now therefore, O ye kings: be instructed, ye judges of the earth.

title: Psalms 2:11
text: Serve the LORD with fear, and rejoice with trembling.

title: Psalms 2:12
text: Kiss the Son, lest he be angry, and ye perish [from] the way, when his wrath is kindled but a little. Blessed [are] all they that put their trust in him.

title: Psalms 3:1
text: ¶<<A Psalm of David, when he fled from Absalom his son.>> LORD, how are they increased that trouble me! many [are] they that rise up against me.

title: Psalms 3:2
text: Many [there be] which say of my soul, [There is] no help for him in God. Selah.

title: Psalms 3:3
text: But thou, O LORD, [art] a shield for me; my glory, and the lifter up of mine head. {for: or, about}

title: Psalms 3:4
text: ¶I cried unto the LORD with my voice, and he heard me out of his holy hill. Selah.

title: Psalms 3:5
text: I laid me down and slept; I awaked; for the LORD sustained me.

title: Psalms 3:6
text: I will not be afraid of ten thousands of people, that have set [themselves] against me round about.

title: Psalms 3:7
text: Arise, O LORD; save me, O my God: for thou hast smitten all mine enemies [upon] the cheek bone; thou hast broken the teeth of the ungodly.

title: Psalms 3:8
text: Salvation [belongeth] unto the LORD: thy blessing [is] upon thy people. Selah.

title: Psalms 4:1
text: ¶<<To the chief Musician on Neginoth, A Psalm of David.>> Hear me when I call, O God of my righteousness: thou hast enlarged me [when I was] in distress; have mercy upon me, and hear my prayer. {chief...: or, overseer} {have...: or, be gracious unto me}

title: Psalms 4:2
text: O ye sons of men, how long [will ye turn] my glory into shame? [how long] will ye love vanity, [and] seek after leasing? Selah.

title: Psalms 4:3
text: But know that the LORD hath set apart him that is godly for himself: the LORD will hear when I call unto him.

title: Psalms 4:4
text: Stand in awe, and sin not: commune with your own heart upon your bed, and be still. Selah.

title: Psalms 4:5
text: Offer the sacrifices of righteousness, and put your trust in the LORD.

title: Psalms 4:6
text: ¶[There be] many that say, Who will shew us [any] good? LORD, lift thou up the light of thy countenance upon us.

title: Psalms 4:7
text: Thou hast put gladness in my heart, more than in the time [that] their corn and their wine increased.

title: Psalms 4:8
text: I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for thou, LORD, only makest me dwell in safety.

title: Psalms 5:1
text: ¶<<To the chief Musician upon Nehiloth, A Psalm of David.>> Give ear to my words, O LORD, consider my meditation.

title: Psalms 5:2
text: Hearken unto the voice of my cry, my King, and my God: for unto thee will I pray.

title: Psalms 5:3
text: My voice shalt thou hear in the morning, O LORD; in the morning will I direct [my prayer] unto thee, and will look up.

title: Psalms 5:4
text: For thou [art] not a God that hath pleasure in wickedness: neither shall evil dwell with thee.

title: Psalms 5:5
text: The foolish shall not stand in thy sight: thou hatest all workers of iniquity. {in...: Heb. before thine eyes}

title: Psalms 5:6
text: Thou shalt destroy them that speak leasing: the LORD will abhor the bloody and deceitful man. {bloody...: Heb. man of bloods and deceit}

title: Psalms 5:7
text: ¶But as for me, I will come [into] thy house in the multitude of thy mercy: [and] in thy fear will I worship toward thy holy temple. {thy holy...: Heb. the temple of thy holiness}

title: Psalms 5:8
text: Lead me, O LORD, in thy righteousness because of mine enemies; make thy way straight before my face. {mine...: Heb. those which observe me}

title: Psalms 5:9
text: For [there is] no faithfulness in their mouth; their inward part [is] very wickedness; their throat [is] an open sepulchre; they flatter with their tongue. {faithfulness: or, stedfastness} {their mouth: Heb. his mouth, that is, the mouth of any of them} {very...: Heb. wickednesses}

title: Psalms 5:10
text: Destroy thou them, O God; let them fall by their own counsels; cast them out in the multitude of their transgressions; for they have rebelled against thee. {Destroy...: or, Make them guilty} {by...: or, from their counsels}

title: Psalms 5:11
text: But let all those that put their trust in thee rejoice: let them ever shout for joy, because thou defendest them: let them also that love thy name be joyful in thee. {defendest...: Heb. coverest over, or, protectest them}

title: Psalms 5:12
text: For thou, LORD, wilt bless the righteous; with favour wilt thou compass him as [with] a shield. {compass: Heb. crown}

title: Psalms 6:1
text: ¶<<To the chief Musician on Neginoth upon Sheminith, A Psalm of David.>> O LORD, rebuke me not in thine anger, neither chasten me in thy hot displeasure. {chief...: or, overseer} {Sheminith: or, the eighth}

title: Psalms 6:2
text: Have mercy upon me, O LORD; for I [am] weak: O LORD, heal me; for my bones are vexed.

title: Psalms 6:3
text: My soul is also sore vexed: but thou, O LORD, how long?

title: Psalms 6:4
text: Return, O LORD, deliver my soul: oh save me for thy mercies' sake.

title: Psalms 6:5
text: For in death [there is] no remembrance of thee: in the grave who shall give thee thanks?

title: Psalms 6:6
text: I am weary with my groaning; all the night make I my bed to swim; I water my couch with my tears. {all...: or, every night}

title: Psalms 6:7
text: Mine eye is consumed because of grief; it waxeth old because of all mine enemies.

title: Psalms 6:8
text: ¶Depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity; for the LORD hath heard the voice of my weeping.

title: Psalms 6:9
text: The LORD hath heard my supplication; the LORD will receive my prayer.

title: Psalms 6:10
text: Let all mine enemies be ashamed and sore vexed: let them return [and] be ashamed suddenly.

title: Psalms 7:1
text: ¶<<Shiggaion of David, which he sang unto the LORD, concerning the words of Cush the Benjamite.>> O LORD my God, in thee do I put my trust: save me from all them that persecute me, and deliver me: {words: or, business}

title: Psalms 7:2
text: Lest he tear my soul like a lion, rending [it] in pieces, while [there is] none to deliver. {none...: Heb. not a deliverer}

title: Psalms 7:3
text: O LORD my God, if I have done this; if there be iniquity in my hands;

title: Psalms 7:4
text: If I have rewarded evil unto him that was at peace with me; (yea, I have delivered him that without cause is mine enemy:)

title: Psalms 7:5
text: Let the enemy persecute my soul, and take [it]; yea, let him tread down my life upon the earth, and lay mine honour in the dust. Selah.

title: Psalms 7:6
text: Arise, O LORD, in thine anger, lift up thyself because of the rage of mine enemies: and awake for me [to] the judgment [that] thou hast commanded.

title: Psalms 7:7
text: So shall the congregation of the people compass thee about: for their sakes therefore return thou on high.

title: Psalms 7:8
text: The LORD shall judge the people: judge me, O LORD, according to my righteousness, and according to mine integrity [that is] in me.

title: Psalms 7:9
text: Oh let the wickedness of the wicked come to an end; but establish the just: for the righteous God trieth the hearts and reins.

title: Psalms 7:10
text: ¶My defence [is] of God, which saveth the upright in heart. {My...: Heb. My buckler is upon God}

title: Psalms 7:11
text: God judgeth the righteous, and God is angry [with the wicked] every day. {judgeth...: or, is a righteous judge}

title: Psalms 7:12
text: If he turn not, he will whet his sword; he hath bent his bow, and made it ready.

title: Psalms 7:13
text: He hath also prepared for him the instruments of death; he ordaineth his arrows against the persecutors.

title: Psalms 7:14
text: Behold, he travaileth with iniquity, and hath conceived mischief, and brought forth falsehood.

title: Psalms 7:15
text: He made a pit, and digged it, and is fallen into the ditch [which] he made. {He made a pit: Heb. He hath digged a pit}

title: Psalms 7:16
text: His mischief shall return upon his own head, and his violent dealing shall come down upon his own pate.

title: Psalms 7:17
text: I will praise the LORD according to his righteousness: and will sing praise to the name of the LORD most high.

title: Psalms 8:1
text: ¶<<To the chief Musician upon Gittith, A Psalm of David.>> O LORD our Lord, how excellent [is] thy name in all the earth! who hast set thy glory above the heavens.

title: Psalms 8:2
text: Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings hast thou ordained strength because of thine enemies, that thou mightest still the enemy and the avenger. {ordained: Heb. founded}

title: Psalms 8:3
text: ¶When I consider thy heavens, the work of thy fingers, the moon and the stars, which thou hast ordained;

title: Psalms 8:4
text: What is man, that thou art mindful of him? and the son of man, that thou visitest him?

title: Psalms 8:5
text: For thou hast made him a little lower than the angels, and hast crowned him with glory and honour.

title: Psalms 8:6
text: Thou madest him to have dominion over the works of thy hands; thou hast put all [things] under his feet:

title: Psalms 8:7
text: All sheep and oxen, yea, and the beasts of the field; {All...: Heb. Flocks and oxen all of them}

title: Psalms 8:8
text: The fowl of the air, and the fish of the sea, [and whatsoever] passeth through the paths of the seas.

title: Psalms 8:9
text: O LORD our Lord, how excellent [is] thy name in all the earth!

title: Psalms 9:1
text: ¶<<To the chief Musician upon Muthlabben, A Psalm of David.>> I will praise [thee], O LORD, with my whole heart; I will shew forth all thy marvellous works.

title: Psalms 9:2
text: I will be glad and rejoice in thee: I will sing praise to thy name, O thou most High.

title: Psalms 9:3
text: When mine enemies are turned back, they shall fall and perish at thy presence.

title: Psalms 9:4
text: For thou hast maintained my right and my cause; thou satest in the throne judging right. {maintained...: Heb. made my judgment} {judging right: Heb. judging in righteousness}

title: Psalms 9:5
text: Thou hast rebuked the heathen, thou hast destroyed the wicked, thou hast put out their name for ever and ever.

title: Psalms 9:6
text: O thou enemy, destructions are come to a perpetual end: and thou hast destroyed cities; their memorial is perished with them. {O thou...: or, The destructions of the enemy are come to a perpetual end: and their cities hast thou destroyed, etc}

title: Psalms 9:7
text: But the LORD shall endure for ever: he hath prepared his throne for judgment.

title: Psalms 9:8
text: And he shall judge the world in righteousness, he shall minister judgment to the people in uprightness.

title: Psalms 9:9
text: The LORD also will be a refuge for the oppressed, a refuge in times of trouble. {a refuge: Heb. an high place}

title: Psalms 9:10
text: And they that know thy name will put their trust in thee: for thou, LORD, hast not forsaken them that seek thee.

title: Psalms 9:11
text: ¶Sing praises to the LORD, which dwelleth in Zion: declare among the people his doings.

title: Psalms 9:12
text: When he maketh inquisition for blood, he remembereth them: he forgetteth not the cry of the humble. {humble: or, afflicted}

title: Psalms 9:13
text: Have mercy upon me, O LORD; consider my trouble [which I suffer] of them that hate me, thou that liftest me up from the gates of death:

title: Psalms 9:14
text: That I may shew forth all thy praise in the gates of the daughter of Zion: I will rejoice in thy salvation.

title: Psalms 9:15
text: The heathen are sunk down in the pit [that] they made: in the net which they hid is their own foot taken.

title: Psalms 9:16
text: The LORD is known [by] the judgment [which] he executeth: the wicked is snared in the work of his own hands. Higgaion. Selah. {Higgaion: that is, Meditation}

title: Psalms 9:17
text: The wicked shall be turned into hell, [and] all the nations that forget God.

title: Psalms 9:18
text: For the needy shall not alway be forgotten: the expectation of the poor shall [not] perish for ever.

title: Psalms 9:19
text: Arise, O LORD; let not man prevail: let the heathen be judged in thy sight.

title: Psalms 9:20
text: Put them in fear, O LORD: [that] the nations may know themselves [to be but] men. Selah.

title: Psalms 10:1
text: ¶Why standest thou afar off, O LORD? [why] hidest thou [thyself] in times of trouble?

title: Psalms 10:2
text: The wicked in [his] pride doth persecute the poor: let them be taken in the devices that they have imagined. {The wicked...: Heb. In the pride of the wicked he doth persecute}

title: Psalms 10:3
text: For the wicked boasteth of his heart's desire, and blesseth the covetous, [whom] the LORD abhorreth. {heart's: Heb. soul's} {blesseth...: or, the covetous blesseth himself, he abhorreth the LORD}

title: Psalms 10:4
text: The wicked, through the pride of his countenance, will not seek [after God]: God [is] not in all his thoughts. {God is...: or, all his thoughts are, There is no God}

title: Psalms 10:5
text: His ways are always grievous; thy judgments [are] far above out of his sight: [as for] all his enemies, he puffeth at them.

title: Psalms 10:6
text: He hath said in his heart, I shall not be moved: for [I shall] never [be] in adversity. {never: Heb. unto generation and generation}

title: Psalms 10:7
text: His mouth is full of cursing and deceit and fraud: under his tongue [is] mischief and vanity. {deceit: Heb. deceits} {vanity: or, iniquity}

title: Psalms 10:8
text: He sitteth in the lurking places of the villages: in the secret places doth he murder the innocent: his eyes are privily set against the poor. {are...: Heb. hide themselves}

title: Psalms 10:9
text: He lieth in wait secretly as a lion in his den: he lieth in wait to catch the poor: he doth catch the poor, when he draweth him into his net. {secretly: Heb. in the secret places}

title: Psalms 10:10
text: He croucheth, [and] humbleth himself, that the poor may fall by his strong ones. {He...: Heb. He breaketh himself} {by...: or, into his strong parts}

title: Psalms 10:11
text: He hath said in his heart, God hath forgotten: he hideth his face; he will never see [it].

title: Psalms 10:12
text: ¶Arise, O LORD; O God, lift up thine hand: forget not the humble. {humble: or, afflicted}

title: Psalms 10:13
text: Wherefore doth the wicked contemn God? he hath said in his heart, Thou wilt not require [it].

title: Psalms 10:14
text: Thou hast seen [it]; for thou beholdest mischief and spite, to requite [it] with thy hand: the poor committeth himself unto thee; thou art the helper of the fatherless. {committeth: Heb. leaveth}

title: Psalms 10:15
text: Break thou the arm of the wicked and the evil [man]: seek out his wickedness [till] thou find none.

title: Psalms 10:16
text: The LORD [is] King for ever and ever: the heathen are perished out of his land.

title: Psalms 10:17
text: LORD, thou hast heard the desire of the humble: thou wilt prepare their heart, thou wilt cause thine ear to hear: {prepare: or, establish}

title: Psalms 10:18
text: To judge the fatherless and the oppressed, that the man of the earth may no more oppress. {oppress: or, terrify}

title: Psalms 11:1
text: ¶<<To the chief Musician, [A Psalm] of David.>> In the LORD put I my trust: how say ye to my soul, Flee [as] a bird to your mountain?

title: Psalms 11:2
text: For, lo, the wicked bend [their] bow, they make ready their arrow upon the string, that they may privily shoot at the upright in heart. {privily: Heb. in darkness}

title: Psalms 11:3
text: If the foundations be destroyed, what can the righteous do?

title: Psalms 11:4
text: ¶The LORD [is] in his holy temple, the LORD'S throne [is] in heaven: his eyes behold, his eyelids try, the children of men.

title: Psalms 11:5
text: The LORD trieth the righteous: but the wicked and him that loveth violence his soul hateth.

title: Psalms 11:6
text: Upon the wicked he shall rain snares, fire and brimstone, and an horrible tempest: [this shall be] the portion of their cup. {an horrible...: or, a burning tempest}

title: Psalms 11:7
text: For the righteous LORD loveth righteousness; his countenance doth behold the upright.

title: Psalms 12:1
text: ¶<<To the chief Musician upon Sheminith, A Psalm of David.>> Help, LORD; for the godly man ceaseth; for the faithful fail from among the children of men. {upon...: or, upon the eighth} {Help: or, Save}

title: Psalms 12:2
text: They speak vanity every one with his neighbour: [with] flattering lips [and] with a double heart do they speak. {a double...: Heb. an heart and an heart}

title: Psalms 12:3
text: The LORD shall cut off all flattering lips, [and] the tongue that speaketh proud things: {proud: Heb. great}

title: Psalms 12:4
text: Who have said, With our tongue will we prevail; our lips [are] our own: who [is] lord over us? {are...: Heb. are with us}

title: Psalms 12:5
text: For the oppression of the poor, for the sighing of the needy, now will I arise, saith the LORD; I will set [him] in safety [from him that] puffeth at him. {puffeth...: or, would ensnare him}

title: Psalms 12:6
text: The words of the LORD [are] pure words: [as] silver tried in a furnace of earth, purified seven times.

title: Psalms 12:7
text: Thou shalt keep them, O LORD, thou shalt preserve them from this generation for ever. {them from: Heb. him, etc: that is, every one of them, etc}

title: Psalms 12:8
text: The wicked walk on every side, when the vilest men are exalted. {men: Heb. of the sons of the men}

title: Psalms 13:1
text: ¶<<To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David.>> How long wilt thou forget me, O LORD? for ever? how long wilt thou hide thy face from me? {chief...: or, overseer}

title: Psalms 13:2
text: How long shall I take counsel in my soul, [having] sorrow in my heart daily? how long shall mine enemy be exalted over me?

title: Psalms 13:3
text: Consider [and] hear me, O LORD my God: lighten mine eyes, lest I sleep the [sleep of] death;

title: Psalms 13:4
text: Lest mine enemy say, I have prevailed against him; [and] those that trouble me rejoice when I am moved.

title: Psalms 13:5
text: But I have trusted in thy mercy; my heart shall rejoice in thy salvation.

title: Psalms 13:6
text: I will sing unto the LORD, because he hath dealt bountifully with me.

title: Psalms 14:1
text: ¶<<To the chief Musician, [A Psalm] of David.>> The fool hath said in his heart, [There is] no God. They are corrupt, they have done abominable works, [there is] none that doeth good.

title: Psalms 14:2
text: The LORD looked down from heaven upon the children of men, to see if there were any that did understand, [and] seek God.

title: Psalms 14:3
text: They are all gone aside, they are [all] together become filthy: [there is] none that doeth good, no, not one. {filthy: Heb. stinking}

title: Psalms 14:4
text: ¶Have all the workers of iniquity no knowledge? who eat up my people [as] they eat bread, and call not upon the LORD.

title: Psalms 14:5
text: There were they in great fear: for God [is] in the generation of the righteous. {were...: Heb. they feared a fear}

title: Psalms 14:6
text: Ye have shamed the counsel of the poor, because the LORD [is] his refuge.

title: Psalms 14:7
text: Oh that the salvation of Israel [were come] out of Zion! when the LORD bringeth back the captivity of his people, Jacob shall rejoice, [and] Israel shall be glad. {Oh...: Heb. Who will give}

title: Psalms 15:1
text: ¶<<A Psalm of David.>> LORD, who shall abide in thy tabernacle? who shall dwell in thy holy hill? {abide: Heb. sojourn}

title: Psalms 15:2
text: He that walketh uprightly, and worketh righteousness, and speaketh the truth in his heart.

title: Psalms 15:3
text: [He that] backbiteth not with his tongue, nor doeth evil to his neighbour, nor taketh up a reproach against his neighbour. {taketh...: or, receiveth, or, endureth}

title: Psalms 15:4
text: In whose eyes a vile person is contemned; but he honoureth them that fear the LORD. [He that] sweareth to [his own] hurt, and changeth not.

title: Psalms 15:5
text: [He that] putteth not out his money to usury, nor taketh reward against the innocent. He that doeth these [things] shall never be moved.

title: Psalms 16:1
text: ¶<<Michtam of David.>> Preserve me, O God: for in thee do I put my trust. {Michtam: or, A golden Psalm}

title: Psalms 16:2
text: [O my soul], thou hast said unto the LORD, Thou [art] my Lord: my goodness [extendeth] not to thee;

title: Psalms 16:3
text: [But] to the saints that [are] in the earth, and [to] the excellent, in whom [is] all my delight.

title: Psalms 16:4
text: Their sorrows shall be multiplied [that] hasten [after] another [god]: their drink offerings of blood will I not offer, nor take up their names into my lips. {hasten...: or, give gifts to another}

title: Psalms 16:5
text: The LORD [is] the portion of mine inheritance and of my cup: thou maintainest my lot. {of mine...: Heb. of my part}

title: Psalms 16:6
text: The lines are fallen unto me in pleasant [places]; yea, I have a goodly heritage.

title: Psalms 16:7
text: I will bless the LORD, who hath given me counsel: my reins also instruct me in the night seasons.

title: Psalms 16:8
text: ¶I have set the LORD always before me: because [he is] at my right hand, I shall not be moved.

title: Psalms 16:9
text: Therefore my heart is glad, and my glory rejoiceth: my flesh also shall rest in hope. {rest...: Heb. dwell confidently}

title: Psalms 16:10
text: For thou wilt not leave my soul in hell; neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption.

title: Psalms 16:11
text: Thou wilt shew me the path of life: in thy presence [is] fulness of joy; at thy right hand [there are] pleasures for evermore.

title: Psalms 17:1
